replies.author: flourishdev
replies.text:
gin And is there anything additional I can do at.the user level to give up less?

You could try using something like RethinkDNS to block connections to Google that aren't needed for functionality although this is not a robust way to prevent Google from getting your data.

There's a few simple steps the apps could take to make DNS blocking completely ineffective and a few apps already do this. It shouldn't hurt, and most apps don't take these steps.

Just know what you input as the user into the app along with it's large permissions are what are going to be a much larger aspects for them to misuse your data than telemetry and the like, so you might consider using email aliasing and fake info when possible.

replies.author: Winston
replies.text: It will take time for it to sink in. You'll hear something a million times and then one day it will click because your knowledge base will slowly have been growing. But to (somewhat) address your question, google on vanilla android is so deeply integrated into the OS it has eyes and ears everywhere. On graphene it does not have that all-powerful access, it is just another app - granted just enough to work. On stock you are giving up everything. On GOS you can go pretty much under the radar depending on how careful you are, but going psuedo and keeping it minimal without trying to be a ghost will save your mind (your normie daily-driver is not the place to hide(edit: as far as being paranoid(in my opinion))). You'll be learning a lot, have fun. Others will come in and give you a lot of the technicals you might be after; if not, use the search!
